One-sentence judgment: transit and intercity bus drivers are not "just driving the vehicle away," but carrying passengers on approved routes and schedules and being responsible for driving safety, passenger service, and operating records. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET-SOC 53-3052.00, which O*NET lists as Job Zone 1-2 (preparation from little to some, SVP below 6.0), and Bright Outlook is not marked. The core boundary is: you may independently complete pre-departure inspections, drive per route and schedule, announce stops, sell tickets and assist passengers, record fares and driving logs, and report delays and accidents per procedures; but you may not change approved routes, stops, or fares on your own, may not replace the operating unit's production safety management judgment, and may not drive commercially when not meeting the required vehicle class and practice qualification requirements.

Signals to keep exploring: your interest in "delivering a group of people safely and on time per the schedule" is greater than in "whether the route is new"; you are willing to maintain attention for long periods and verify the vehicle and route per procedures; you can stay steady under congestion, bad weather, passenger emotions, and time pressure and insist on handling anomalies and reporting accidents per procedures; you accept long periods of sitting, an enclosed cabin, noise, and frequent public contact, and are willing to keep updating safety and emergency knowledge.

Conditions for pausing high-cost investment first: you have not yet, while holding the driving license for the corresponding vehicle class, completed under mentoring or supervision a full closed loop from pre-departure inspection, on-schedule operation, stop announcements and passenger service, anomaly handling, to end-of-shift records and fare handover; or you only want to drive and are unwilling to inspect the vehicle and keep records per procedures, and unwilling to face passenger disputes and emergencies; also, do not treat "can drive a car" as proof that you can drive a commercial bus or already hold the practice qualification.

Education, qualifications, and authorization must be verified separately: O*NET lists this occupation's preparation level as Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), usually requiring a high school diploma or equivalent or GED, with on-the-job training from a few days to a year; in the United States, bus drivers usually need a commercial driver's license (CDL) and must meet driving record, medical examination, vision and hearing, and background check requirements; in mainland China, drivers engaged in commercial road passenger transport must hold the corresponding motor vehicle driving license for more than 1 year, be no older than 63, have no major or greater at-fault traffic accident within 3 years, master road passenger transport regulations and basic passenger first aid knowledge, and pass an examination to obtain the corresponding practice qualification certificate (Provisions on the Administration of Road Transport Practitioners); urban public bus and trolleybus drivers must also hold a motor vehicle driving license matching the vehicle class with the internship period completed, and have no violation record of 12 points or more in the most recent 3 consecutive scoring cycles, among others (Provisions on the Administration of Urban Public Bus and Trolleybus Passenger Transport).

One sentence: this is a position centered on safe driving, passenger transport service, vehicle inspection, and operating records, and its outputs are reviewable driving and fare records, transport service completed per schedule, and anomaly information reported and escalated per procedures; it is not a role that decides routes and fares on its own, nor does it replace the operating unit's production safety responsibility. The U.S. wage, employment, and projection data use this occupation's basis, Bus Drivers, Transit and Intercity (SOC 53-3052); for mainland China, the evidence routing does not publish occupation-level or proxy wage figures for this occupation, keeping only the statistical basis and the gap.

The work of this occupation can be divided into three categories: first, safe driving and operations (driving per the schedule and approved route, stopping properly, obeying traffic laws, adjusting to weather and road conditions, and ensuring passengers ride smoothly and safely); second, passenger service and ticketing (announcing routes and stops, assisting elderly or disabled passengers and others, collecting tickets and fares, reminding passengers to maintain order, answering questions about schedules and routes, and handling passenger emergencies or service disruptions); third, vehicle inspection and record handover (inspecting the vehicle and fuel, oil, and water levels before departure, keeping the vehicle clean, recording fares and driving information and maintaining the log, reporting delays and accidents, and completing end-of-shift and fare and vehicle condition handover). All three share the same work chain centered on safe driving and reviewable records.
Safe driving and operations

Depart per the schedule and approved route → stop properly at stops and load and unload passengers → obey traffic laws and drive smoothly → adjust speed and following distance to road and weather conditions → ensure passengers ride smoothly and safely → complete handover per the shift requirements on arrival.
Passenger service and ticketing

Announce routes and stops → assist elderly or disabled passengers and others in boarding and alighting → answer questions about schedules and routes → collect tickets or cash fares and apply the fare rules → remind passengers to be seated and maintain order in the cabin → handle passenger emergencies or service disruptions and report promptly.

Inspect the vehicle before departure and check gasoline, oil, and water levels, record fares and driving information per shift and maintain the log, keep the vehicle clean, report delays or accidents per procedures, and complete end-of-shift handover of fares and vehicle condition.

Transit and intercity bus drivers produce passenger transport completed per schedule; school bus drivers address student commuting with different requirements for minor supervision and school procedures; shuttle and limousine drivers address hotel, airport, and corporate transfers with different service objects and shift patterns; taxi drivers operate on meter per passenger instructions, generally not on fixed routes and schedules; rail locomotive drivers and subway and tram drivers work on fixed rail systems with different qualifications and signal rules; baggage porters and bellhops only handle baggage and lobby service and do not drive vehicles. Similar names or working in the same transport industry do not mean qualifications, responsibility boundaries, and operating models are interchangeable.
Core purpose

Transport passengers per the schedule and traffic and safety specifications, perform vehicle inspection, service, and records well, and support safety and punctuality, without guaranteeing the elimination of all risk.
Main objects and basis

The objects are transit buses and long-distance coaches and their passengers, routes, stops, and shift arrangements; the basis is road traffic safety law and vehicle class requirements, the operating unit's driving work plans and service specifications, vehicle inspection and driving record systems, and fare and concessionary travel rules (in mainland China also the Regulations on Road Transport of the People's Republic of China, the Provisions on the Administration of Road Transport Practitioners, the Provisions on the Administration of Road Passenger Transport and Passenger Stations, and the Provisions on the Administration of Urban Public Bus and Trolleybus Passenger Transport).
Core process

Pre-departure inspection and preparation, driving and stopping per the schedule and route, stop announcements and passenger service, ticket and fare collection, anomaly and emergency handling, records and reporting, and end-of-shift handover of fares and vehicle.
Main outputs

Transport service completed per schedule, complete and reviewable driving logs and fare records, delay and accident report records, vehicle inspection and cleaning results, and end-of-shift and handover documents completed per procedures.
Responsible parties

Driving safety and passenger service are the driver's responsibility; shift scheduling and route and stop adjustments are decided by the operating unit and the competent department; the primary responsibility for production safety is borne by the operating enterprise; reporting and handling of accidents, violations, and passenger complaints follow institutional rules and applicable provisions; judgments beyond your own duties and authorization must be escalated per procedures.
Authority and approval

Changes to ordinary routes, stops, and time periods follow operating management procedures; Article 22 of the 2024 urban regulation has emergency and safety exceptions, and Article 34 permits suspending the relevant operation when unsafe. Drivers follow current emergency procedures to protect passengers promptly, handle the situation, and report, and Article 29 of the 2017 rules prohibits abandoning the vehicle and fleeing before the passengers; emergency protection should not be delayed to await approval for an ordinary change. In China, drivers engaged in commercial road passenger transport follow Article 9 of the 2026 practice provisions: the corresponding motor vehicle driving license for at least 1 year, age no older than 63, no major or greater at-fault traffic accident within 3 years, mastery of road passenger transport regulations and basic motor vehicle repair and passenger first aid knowledge, and passing an examination to obtain the corresponding practice qualification. 63 is not the age threshold for all motor vehicle driving licenses, and urban bus positions are verified separately under urban rules.
Conclusion boundary

The driving log and fare records state "what transport this shift completed per plan and what anomalies occurred"; they do not equal a determination of accident responsibility, nor do they replace the operating unit's safety management judgment and the competent department's regulatory conclusions, and they will change with review and subsequent handling.

Before onboarding, verify at least six items: the position basis and form of employment (bus enterprise, road passenger transport enterprise, charter or tourist transport, or outsourcing), shift and schedule arrangements (including early and last shifts and holidays), vehicle class and practice qualification requirements, fixed or rotating route and vehicle model arrangements, safety and occupational health protection arrangements (including emergency handling procedures), and the real pay method (hours, shift allowances, and performance basis).
Occupational basis

The 2022 Classification Code of Occupations, 4-02-02-01 passenger vehicle driver, includes bus drivers and urban public bus and trolleybus drivers, and also taxi and ride-hailing drivers, a scope broader than U.S. 53-3052. 4-02-02-03 road passenger transport attendant handles ticket sales and inspection and on-board service and is not a synonymous detailed class for drivers; verify against actual tasks. O*NET2025 industries: government 59%, transportation and warehousing 37%, other 4%; this is the occupational industry distribution, not wages or the Chinese bus unit industry. The OOH separately details local government (excluding education and hospitals) 54%, urban transit 17%, charter 8%, intercity and rural 5%, and other passenger transport 3%, which cannot be forcibly merged.
Education and training pathway

O*NET new-entrant education Q&A: 84% high school or equivalent, 13% less than high school, and 2% postsecondary certificate, which is not the composition of current practitioners. JobZone1—2/SVP below 6 with a few days to one year is a preparation range summary; the BLS typical entry for this occupation is a high school diploma / None related experience / medium-term on-the-job training. U.S. bus drivers need a CDL and the applicable P passenger endorsement, issued by the state, verified by vehicle class and state rules; entry-level A/B or initial P, among others, require separate verification of ELDT applicability and exceptions.
Methods and tools

The detailed profile lists 3 software categories: browsers, map creation (MapQuest/MapPoint), and operating systems; the Hot list is 1 specific product, Windows, with hiring mention percentages NA (not 0). Category counts, product counts, hiring mentions, and AI deployment rates are interpreted separately.
Safety and work permits

Work risks mainly involve long periods of sitting and repetitive motion, an enclosed cabin and noise, outdoor exposure in all kinds of weather, contact with emotionally agitated passengers, exposure to disease or infection, and the consequences of traffic accidents and emergencies; O*NET work context shows 87% sit continuously or almost continuously, 82% use their hands to handle objects and tools continuously or almost continuously, 85% work inside an enclosed vehicle every day, 74% are in constant contact with others, 64% face time pressure every day, 61% say the consequences of error are extremely serious, and 83% are on a regular schedule; pre-departure inspections should be completed per procedures, driving should follow vehicle class and practice qualification requirements, emergencies should be handled per institutional procedures, and protection and emergency equipment should be used as the position requires.
Training and regulatory requirements

In China, drivers engaged in commercial road passenger transport follow Article 9 of the 2026 practice provisions: the corresponding motor vehicle driving license for at least 1 year, age no older than 63, no major or greater at-fault traffic accident within 3 years, mastery of road passenger transport regulations and basic motor vehicle repair and passenger first aid knowledge, and passing an examination to obtain the corresponding practice qualification. 63 is not the age threshold for all motor vehicle driving licenses, and urban bus positions are verified separately under urban rules. Urban buses are verified under Articles 31—32 of the 2024 regulation and Articles 27—28 of the 2017 rules for duty capability, health, no violent crime or drug record, a matching driving license with the driving probationary period completed, no full 12 points in 3 consecutive scoring cycles, and no traffic accident crime, dangerous driving crime, or drink-driving record; training and assessment must be passed before taking up the post, archives must be kept for inspection, and filing with the competent department is made per the rules.
Pay and working hours

Editorial verification: shifts, early and last shifts and holidays, overtime and allowances, the pay method, and who bears training and certification costs are verified against the target employer's contract; no specific recruitment frequency was verified in this round.

Transit and intercity bus drivers (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 53-3052.00, Bus Drivers, Transit and Intercity) drive transit buses or long-distance coaches, including regular route operation, charter, and private transport; the official description includes possibly assisting passengers with baggage and possibly collecting tickets or fares. Daily work includes: driving the vehicle along a specified route or to a specified destination per the schedule and obeying traffic laws, ensuring a smooth and safe trip for passengers; stopping in the loading area to let passengers board and alight and announcing stops to passengers; inspecting the vehicle before departure and checking gasoline, oil, and water levels; assisting elderly or disabled passengers and others in boarding and alighting, confirming they are seated, helping with baggage, and answering questions about schedules and routes; collecting tickets or cash fares from passengers; handling passenger emergencies or service disruptions; reporting delays or accidents; reminding passengers to be seated and keeping order; adjusting heating, lighting, and ventilation systems for passenger comfort; recording cash and ticket revenue and other information and maintaining the driving log; keeping the vehicle clean; reading maps to plan routes; and loading and unloading baggage in the baggage compartment. It bears driving safety and passenger service responsibility, but does not replace the operating unit's production safety responsibility, nor may it decide routes, stops, and fares on its own.

paragraphs: This page compares transit and intercity bus drivers with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference better suits. Adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupation descriptions, and do not mean trade names are interchangeable.

Evidence note: the career directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 53-3052.00 and the adjacent entries (U.S. basis); the vehicle class, practice qualifications, and safety requirements of adjacent trades must be verified separately under their own jurisdictions, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares the directional differences between transit and intercity bus drivers and adjacent trades; the basis for judgment is the main outputs, the parties responsible to, and the qualifications required, rather than the similarity of trade names.

School bus drivers address minors and require additional student supervision and school procedure requirements; this occupation addresses ordinary passengers in transit and intercity transport, with different shift and route patterns.

If you prefer working with primary and secondary school students and following the school calendar, examine school bus drivers first; if you prefer running regular transit or intercity routes, examine this occupation first.
Transport students to and from school and ensure student safety on board, with outputs mainly pickup and drop-off service completed per the school calendar and riding order records.
Bus Drivers, School
School bus monitors do not drive the vehicle and focus on student supervision and order; this occupation centers on driving and passenger service and bears driving safety responsibility.
If you prefer care and order management without driving responsibility, examine school bus monitors first; if you prefer driving a commercial bus, examine this occupation first.
Supervise students on board, assist with boarding and alighting, and maintain order, with outputs mainly safe student escort and order maintenance.
School Bus Monitors
Baggage porters and bellhops only handle baggage and lobby service and do not drive vehicles or bear driving safety responsibility; this occupation centers on driving and passenger service.
If you prefer service and carrying work and accept physical load, examine baggage porters and bellhops first; if you prefer driving a vehicle in operation, examine this occupation first.
Carry baggage at stations and hotels, assist travelers, and relay information, with outputs mainly baggage handling and traveler assistance.
Baggage Porters and Bellhops

Reservation and ticket agents handle ticketing and information at a fixed post and do not bear vehicle operation and driving safety; this occupation handles driving, fares, and passenger service on the operational frontline at the same time.

If you prefer ticketing and advisory work, examine reservation and transportation ticket agents and travel clerks first; if you prefer driving on the frontline and serving passengers directly, examine this occupation first.
Handle bookings, ticket issuance, and travel inquiries at a window or online, with outputs mainly ticketing and traveler information records.
Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks

Dispatchers decide routes and capacity arrangements from the back office and do not drive vehicles; this occupation executes transport per dispatch arrangements and is responsible for driving safety, and the two differ in decision authority and responsibility.
If you prefer operational coordination and dispatch decisions, examine dispatchers first; if you prefer driving and serving on the operational frontline, examine this occupation first.
Arrange and adjust shifts, monitor operating status, and coordinate anomaly handling, with outputs mainly dispatch instructions and operating records.
Dispatchers, Except Police, Fire, and Ambulance

Transit and railroad police have enforcement duties and corresponding qualification requirements and do not perform passenger driving tasks; this occupation centers on driving and passenger service and reports and refers violations and safety incidents per procedures.
If you prefer enforcement and safety patrol work, examine transit and railroad police first; if you prefer driving a commercial bus and providing passenger service, examine this occupation first.
Enforce the law, patrol, and handle safety incidents within the transport system, with outputs mainly enforcement and safety incident handling records.
Transit and Railroad Police

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the main outputs, the parties responsible to, and the qualifications required, not how similar the names are; once the direction is set, you should verify item by item the target position's vehicle class and practice qualification requirements, shift and schedule arrangements, route and vehicle model scope, and training and certification arrangements, and keep written confirmation.

Direct answer: the main risks include occupational health problems from long periods of sitting and repetitive motion, exposure to an enclosed cabin and noise, outdoor and road conditions risks in all kinds of weather, the consequences of traffic accidents and emergencies, conflicts with emotionally agitated passengers, and exposure to disease or infection; control depends on safe and defensive driving training, pre-departure inspection and vehicle maintenance, handling emergencies and escalating alarms per procedures, shift and fatigue management, and driving records and after-the-fact debriefs.

Driving continuously without rest to meet the shift, ignoring physical discomfort, or operating while ill.

Road conditions, weather, and traffic accidents may cause personal injury and service disruption, and the consequences of error were rated extremely serious by 61% of respondents.

paragraphs: Qualification boundary: driving experience, vehicle class, practice qualification certificate, employer onboarding assessment, shift authorization, and route operating authority are different states, and none can be automatically inferred from another.

O*NET new-entrant education Q&A: 84% high school or equivalent, 13% less than high school, and 2% postsecondary certificate, which is not the composition of current practitioners. JobZone1—2/SVP below 6 with a few days to one year is a preparation range summary; the BLS typical entry for this occupation is a high school diploma / None related experience / medium-term on-the-job training. U.S. bus drivers need a CDL and the applicable P passenger endorsement, issued by the state, verified by vehicle class and state rules; entry-level A/B or initial P, among others, require separate verification of ELDT applicability and exceptions.

In China, drivers engaged in commercial road passenger transport follow Article 9 of the 2026 practice provisions: the corresponding motor vehicle driving license for at least 1 year, age no older than 63, no major or greater at-fault traffic accident within 3 years, mastery of road passenger transport regulations and basic motor vehicle repair and passenger first aid knowledge, and passing an examination to obtain the corresponding practice qualification. 63 is not the age threshold for all motor vehicle driving licenses, and urban bus positions are verified separately under urban rules. Urban buses are verified under Articles 31—32 of the 2024 regulation and Articles 27—28 of the 2017 rules for duty capability, health, no violent crime or drug record, a matching driving license with the driving probationary period completed, no full 12 points in 3 consecutive scoring cycles, and no traffic accident crime, dangerous driving crime, or drink-driving record; training and assessment must be passed before taking up the post, archives must be kept for inspection, and filing with the competent department is made per the rules.

Before onboarding, verify item by item the vehicle class and practice qualification, shift and route authorization, pre-job training and assessment records, and the shift and pay basis, and keep written confirmation.

Recruitment verification note: no specific job postings were obtained in this round; transit, intercity routes, and charter are editorial job examples and cannot be called verified public recruitment frequency or a uniform sequence.

When reading recruitment information, verify the form of employment (bus enterprise, road passenger transport enterprise, charter or tourist transport, or outsourcing), shift and schedule arrangements, vehicle class and practice qualification requirements, route and vehicle model scope, and hours and pay method, and be wary of wording that markets short-term training as enabling independent driving of a commercial bus or independent decisions on routes and fares.
